terms.comment: Egger’s term, in Morgan–Owens. zōna is classically one of the five belts into which the ancients divided the sky and the earth (quīnque tenent caelum zōnae, Verg. G. 1.233), and temporālis “of time” (mostly post-Augustan); the phrase is modern. For the difference in hours between two places, say it with the hours: see the examples.

phrases.latin: Cum hīc hōra decima est, Lisbōnae nōna est.
phrases.english: When it’s ten o’clock here, it’s nine in Lisbon.

phrases.latin: Lisbōna in aliā zōnā temporālī sita est.
phrases.english: Lisbon is in another time zone.

sources: Lewis & Short: zona · Lewis & Short: temporalis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. time zone.
